newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):

Championship favourites Liverpool aim to bounce back from their 1-0 home defeat against Sheffield Wednesday last Saturday. Midfielder Jamie Redknapp (ankle) and striker Stan Collymore (calf) missed that match but are set to return. Despite selling defender John Scales to Spurs last Sunday Roy Evans' side will be at full strength at the back with Neil Ruddock, Mark Wright and Phil Babb keeping England's Dominic Matteo on the bench.

Middlesbrough's troubled Brazilian star Emerson is expected to play after returning from his third unsanctioned trip to South America since joining the club this season. Compatriot Juninho is still a doubt with knee ligament trouble. Norwegian Jan-Aage Fjortoft is likely to retain his place in attack alongside Fabrizio Ravanelli. Dane Mikkel Beck is doubtful (influenza).

Wimbledon, unbeaten in their last 18 matches, will be without captain Vinnie Jones, who is on international duty with Wales. Brian McAllister takes his place in midfield while Robbie Earle will wear the captain's arm-band. Goalkeeper Paul Heald (ankle) and England under-21 captain Ben Thatcher (ankle) are still out.

Blackburn, starting to draw away from the bottom three, drew 1-1 at Leicester last week. Striker Chris Sutton looks to extend his run of four goals in five games. Midfielder Garry Flitcroft is out for two weeks with an ankle injury.

Leeds, looking for their fifth clean sheet in six games, will again start with Ghanian striker Tony Yeboah on the bench, even though he has recovered from a knee injury which sidelined him for eight months. Manager George Graham keeps faith in the attacking partnership of Brian Deane and Ian Rush. Norwegian international Gunnar Halle is set to make his debut for the Yorkshire side after signing from Oldham.

Spurs' striker Chris Armstrong is out until the start of February with a suspected infection of his left ankle tendon. John Scales will travel with the Londoners to Elland Road, but is unlikely to play. Scales was on the verge of joining Leeds at the weekend before Tottenham stole him away to White Hart Lane. England midfielder Darren Anderton is still out (knee).

Sunderland, who lost 3-1 at home to Wimbledon last weekend, are still without injured goalkeeper Tony Coton, Irish striker Niall Quinn and defender Lee Howey. Polish international Dariusz Kubicki is expected to start at right back with former Chelsea player Gareth Hall at left back.

Chelsea striker Mark Hughes faces the possibility of two games in 24 hours, just a fortnight after receiveing eight stitches in a gash in his right shin. He could play for Wales against Turkey in Cardiff on Saturday and then fly up to Sunderland for Sunday's league match. Italian Gianluca Vialli (hamstring) is out.
